Empirical Research Plan ― “Does Banking Deregulation Promote Economic Growth?”

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Identification Strategy  

Strategy: Staggered-adoption Difference-in-Differences (DID) with dynamic event-study coefficients estimated à la Sun & Abraham (2021) / Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021).  

Why appropriate:  
• Treatment varies at the state–year level, begins at one clearly dated law change, and never reverses.  
• All states are observed before and after treatment; rich pre-period (1972–deregulation year) allows pre-trend testing.  
• The staggered design yields credible untreated counterfactuals in each year provided parallel-trend assumptions hold.  
• Modern estimators correct the bias that classic TWFE suffers under staggered timing.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2. Treatment and Control Definition  

Treatment variable   : Treat_it = 1 if state i has removed intrastate branching restrictions by year t (inclusive), 0 otherwise.  
Control group        : In each calendar year t, the control units are states that have not yet deregulated (never-treated states play that role for the entire post-period).  
Treatment timing     : DeregYear_i = calendar year the enabling legislation became effective (source: Kroszner-Strahan database). Relative event time k = t – DeregYear_i.  
No RDD, no running variable.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1 Parallel pre-trends: In the absence of deregulation, income/output growth in soon-to-be-treated states would have continued to evolve like that of not-yet-treated states.  
  Plausibility: Political idiosyncrasies (bank-lobby strength, gubernatorial elections) primarily drove adoption timing; economic trends were not systematically different (supported by historical narratives). Empirically testable with pre-period event-time coefficients.  

A2 No anticipation/behavioral response before law becomes effective.  
  Plausibility: Most states prohibited de novo branching until the effective date; banks could not pre-open branches. Use leads to test.  

A3 No spillovers across states (SUTVA).  
  Plausibility: Interstate branching remained illegal; capital cannot easily cross state lines via branches. Still, multi-state holding companies might respond—later robustness addresses this.  

A4 Time-varying shocks are common or fully absorbed by year FEs, or correlate only with controls.  
  Plausibility: National monetary policy, oil shocks, Volcker disinflation, etc. hit all states simultaneously; year fixed effects and region-by-year FEs mitigate.  

A5 Stable composition: No major border changes or systematic migration induced precisely by treatment.  
  Plausibility: State borders fixed; composition changes gradual and can be controlled for.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

4. Main Threats & Mitigation  

T1 Endogenous adoption (states deregulate when growth is slow to stimulate economy).  
   • Include state-specific linear or cubic trends, political controls.  
   • Pre-trend (event-time k ≤ –3..–1) coefficients should be statistically zero.  
   • Exploit “stacked” DID restricting sample to ±10 years around each adoption (Gardner 2022).  

T2 Concurrent policy reforms (e.g., intrastate branching often paired with interstate bank-holding-company entry laws).  
   • Control for interstate banking deregulation indicator.  
   • Drop adoption years where both reforms occur together (robustness).  

T3 Cross-state spillovers through holding-company lending.  
   • Leave-one-out specification: omit bordering states in control pool.  
   • Spatial HAC errors (Conley) to correct inference.  

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

5. R Code Outline (execut-able)

```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)      # fast data
library(fixest)          # TWFE + SA
library(did)             # Callaway & Sant’Anna
library(eventstudyinteract) # Sun & Abraham
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load and merge ------------------------------------------------------
st <- fread("state_panel_1972_1992.csv")   # outcome & controls
dereg <- fread("dereg_dates.csv")          # DeregYear_i
st <- merge(st, dereg, by = "state")

# 2. Variable construction ----------------------------------------------
st[, treat := as.integer(year >= DeregYear)]     # 1 = post-dereg
st[, reltime := year - DeregYear]               # event time k
st[, rel_bin := fifelse(reltime <= -6, -6,
                 fifelse(reltime >= 6, 6, reltime))]  # bins

# 3. Main TWFE (Sun-Abraham) --------------------------------------------
sa_mod <- feols(
  l_income_pc ~ sunab(DeregYear, year) +   # dynamic effects
      educ + urban + pop + indshare + year_trend, 
  cluster = "state",
  data = st,
  fixef = ~ state + year)

iplot(sa_mod, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Years relative to deregulation")

# 4. Callaway & Sant’Anna aggregate ATT ----------------------------------
cs <- att_gt(yname = "l_income_pc",
             tname = "year",
             idname = "state",
             gname = "DeregYear",
             xformla = ~ educ + urban + indshare,
             data = st)
agg_effect <- aggte(cs, type = "group")
summary(agg_effect)

# 5. Robustness: add state trends ----------------------------------------
trend_mod <- feols(
  l_income_pc ~ sunab(DeregYear, year) + educ + urban + pop +
    cspline(year, 2, state),              # cubic state-specific trend
  cluster = "state",
  data = st,
  fixef = ~ state + year)

# 6. Export results ------------------------------------------------------
etable(sa_mod, trend_mod, tex = TRUE, digits = 3)
```

Notes:  
• `l_income_pc` and `l_gsp` are log outcomes; replicate for GSP growth.  
• For Conley-adjusted errors use `fixest::coeftest` with `vcov_conley`.  
• All regressions repeated on growth rates (Δlog) as check.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

6. Expected Results  

Theory predicts a positive effect: better banking competition → lower lending spreads, more credit, better allocation. Prior: +0.5 – 1.0 percentage-point increase in annual per-capita income growth within five years post-deregulation; cumulative 5-year gain ≈ 3 – 5 %. For GSP similar or slightly larger.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
(1 = clearly satisfied; 0 = questionable)

C1 Pre-trends flat?              0.8 (empirically test; likely OK)  
C2 No anticipation?              0.7 (banks may lobby early)  
C3 No spillovers/SUTVA?          0.6 (possible cross-state effects)  
C4 No other simultaneous shocks? 0.7 (control but not perfect)  
C5 Correct inference (clustering, heterogeneous timing bias corrected)? 1.0  

Overall: 3.8 / 5 → credible but must be demonstrated empirically.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
